key_terms.definition: Empirical power-law relationships between test loss and model size, dataset size, and compute, first established by Kaplan et al. (2020).
Compute-optimal allocation rule (Hoffmann et al.) pairing parameter count and training-token count roughly equally for a fixed compute budget.
Three-stage alignment pipeline — supervised fine-tuning, reward-model training on preference pairs, and PPO — that produced InstructGPT.
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that freezes the pretrained weight matrix and learns a low-rank update, cutting trainable parameters sharply.
IO-aware attention kernel that tiles the softmax computation to avoid materializing the full L×L attention matrix in HBM, cutting memory traffic from O(L²) to O(L).
Stored per-token keys and values reused across autoregressive decoding steps; its memory footprint drives attention-variant and paging innovations discussed here.
Serving technique (used in vLLM) that stores the KV cache in non-contiguous physical pages looked up via a block table, eliminating memory fragmentation.
Architecture in which a learned router activates only a subset of expert sub-networks per token, growing total parameters without proportional per-token FLOPs.
Alignment method that reparameterizes the RLHF reward in terms of policy log-probability ratios, yielding a single cross-entropy loss on preference pairs with no separate reward model or RL loop.
Critic-free RL algorithm that samples a group of completions per prompt and normalizes advantages by the group's mean and standard deviation instead of using a value network.
Prompting technique that includes or elicits step-by-step reasoning traces before the final answer, dramatically improving multi-step reasoning at sufficient model scale.
Inference technique where a small draft model proposes several tokens that the target model verifies in one forward pass, yielding multiple accepted tokens per target step.

prerequisites: the RLHF/alignment pipeline at a conceptual level
